label: Game A
nuance_found: Hold COUCH only as the ring turns gold (holding early makes the rival brace and you glance off), let go when a storm cell is under you or the bolt zaps your mast, fly off a wave crest for a charged strike from above (high ground), and keep the white marker inside the gold band so you are not rammed. Barnacle punishes steering into him. There is also a Dock to swap boat and lance.
audio: A looping sea-shanty style music track under everything, plus thunder cracks, a charge whoosh, lance crack and body thud on every hit, wind gusts, splashes, a horn at match start, and a sad defeat sting.
furthest_progress: Squall Cup: beat Pip Tiller (cup screen showed him BEATEN), reached Bosun Barnacle (opponent 2 of 8) and kept losing to him (many defeat stings); late in the session I replayed a Pip match and was ahead 5 pips to 2 in Tilt 8 when time ran out. Never saw opponent 3.
control_trouble: Steering slider is very touchy and I only see it every 0.5 s, so lining up and keeping the marker in gold was mostly luck. Second-finger hold on COUCH often did not register at the first try, and a stuck finger once froze the result-screen buttons for about 40 s (my fault, not the game).
best_moment: First hit on Pip from a crest: CHARGED, a big BOTH HIT burst of splinters and 'you dealt 3, took 1'.
worst_moment: Barnacle: repeated losses to ram shoves and zaps I could not read in time, plus full-screen lightning flashes that hide the controls.
verdict: It looks great and every hit feels like a real moment, and beating Pip felt good. But in 30 seconds I did not understand ring timing, the storm cells and the ram marker, and the text tips are long. Barnacle is a brick wall for a bus-ride player, I got zapped and rammed and did not know why until the third try. I would give it one more go for the drama of the last-pip fights, but I would probably delete it the same day. It is a 5, a good looking 5.
